headline: A lookup table answers from its own entries, so a name taken off the wire cannot resolve to something the table never registered.
summary:
A table written as an ordinary object literal inherits from Object.prototype, so looking a name up in it can return a member nobody put there. Asking such a table for constructor returns a function; asking for any name something else in the process left on Object.prototype returns whatever that is. When the name comes off the wire, the message picks which entry the table answers with. A WebAuthn attestation naming constructor as its format reached the verifier table and was handed Object's own constructor to run as a verifier, and a C509 certificate naming an unregistered public-key algorithm parsed as valid instead of being rejected.

Every module-level table in the toolkit now carries no prototype, from the signature-scheme and content-encryption registries to the name tables pki.C.NAMES exposes. A name the table does not hold answers undefined, which is what each caller's miss handling already expects.

A module-level table declared as an object literal now fails the build, so the next table written that way is caught where it is written.

Fixed: A lookup table carries no prototype, so a name the wire supplies resolves to an entry the table registered or to nothing. Two verbs were reachable: pki.webauthn.verify selected a verifier the table never held for an attestation naming constructor, toString or another Object.prototype member as its format, and pki.schema.c509.parse accepted a certificate whose subject-public-key algorithm named such a member instead of throwing c509/unknown-algorithm. The same change applies to the signature-scheme, content-encryption, key-agreement, extension-decoder and status-name registries.
Changed: Every object the toolkit publishes as a table carries no prototype: pki.C.TIME, pki.C.BYTES, pki.C.LIMITS, pki.C.NAMES and each name table under it, pki.asn1.TAGS, pki.asn1.build, pki.cbor.build, pki.ct.HASH_ALGORITHMS, pki.ct.SIGNATURE_ALGORITHMS, pki.hpke.suites, pki.path.PROCESSED_EXTENSIONS and pki.path.TARGET_UNPROCESSED_IF_CRITICAL. So do the maps a verb returns keyed by names rather than by a fixed set of fields: the results of pki.oid.all, pki.est.paths and pki.scep.parseCapabilities, the headers on each part pki.est.splitMultipartMixed returns, the counts map on a pki.lint.certificate result, and the purposes map on each anchor from pki.trust.parseCertdata, pki.trust.parseCcadbCsv and pki.trust.anchor. Every other result a verb returns, parsed certificates among them, keeps the prototype it had. Reading an entry, calling a member, listing the keys, spreading, destructuring and serializing to JSON are unchanged; calling an Object.prototype method on the object itself, such as table.hasOwnProperty(name), no longer works, so use Object.hasOwn(table, name).
